ml-proust-buffalo-translations.notes: Original publication dates and varying English title, volume, and translator conventions; not a single standard edition.

ml-proust-cambridge-genesis.title: The birth and development of À la recherche du temps perdu, The Cambridge Companion to Proust (Cambridge University Press, 2001)
ml-proust-cambridge-genesis.notes: Dates the genesis around 1908 and work through November 1922; not a claim of full chapter access.

ml-proust-nyrb.title: Peter Brooks, In Search of His Vocation, The New York Review of Books, March 2024
ml-proust-nyrb.notes: Single connected novel published in parts; 1913 first volume; delayed expansion during First World War; text of last installments dependent on editorial interventions. Public excerpt consulted.

ml-proust-wikipedia.title: Wikipedia, In Search of Lost Time
ml-proust-wikipedia.notes: Optional overview and starting place for readers; use institutional and scholarly references for consequential claims.

ml-faulkner-primary-pg.title: William Faulkner, The Sound and the Fury (1929), Project Gutenberg eBook 75170
ml-faulkner-primary-pg.notes: Original 1929 narrative text, four author-dated sections. Public-domain transcription released 2025. Later Compson Appendix not part of this 1929 text. Plot claims are checked against the identified sections; do not infer every date from Benjy or Quentin as certain.

ml-faulkner-digital.title: Digital Yoknapatawpha, University of Virginia: The Sound and the Fury (Text Key 218)

ml-faulkner-temporal.title: Digital Yoknapatawpha, The Art of Faulkner’s Technique: Creating the Chronologies

ml-faulkner-gibson.title: Digital Yoknapatawpha, University of Virginia, Gibson Family
ml-faulkner-gibson.notes: Family relationships and appearances of Dilsey, Versh, Frony, T.P. and Luster. The project openly labels some character-relationship inferences as assumptions.

ml-faulkner-yale6.title: Wai Chee Dimock, Open Yale Courses AMST 246, Lecture 6: The Sound and the Fury
ml-faulkner-yale6.notes: Primary scholarly context for Benjy narration, origin image of Caddy in the tree, sensory associations, and interpretive claims concerning innocence and dependence.

ml-faulkner-yale7.title: Wai Chee Dimock, Open Yale Courses AMST 246, Lecture 7: The Sound and the Fury, Part II
ml-faulkner-yale7.notes: Analyzes Benjy/Quentin variations, Quentin’s relation to Caddy, and racial difference. Interpretations are attributed; not all readings are uncontested facts.

ml-faulkner-yale8.title: Wai Chee Dimock, Open Yale Courses AMST 246, Lecture 8: The Sound and the Fury, Part III
ml-faulkner-yale8.notes: Jason’s narratives of grievance, changing economic scale, modernity and Western Union. Dimock’s qualified sympathy for Jason is an attributed interpretation, not a moral acquittal.

ml-faulkner-appendix.title: Digital Yoknapatawpha, University of Virginia, Appendix: Compson (Text Key 233)
ml-faulkner-appendix.notes: Written in 1945 for The Portable Faulkner (1946). The additional genealogy is not included in the original 1929 narrative; later editions vary on its placement and inclusion.

ml-faulkner-author-italics.title: Faulkner at Virginia, transcription of William Faulkner’s discussion of italics and colors (wfaudio09_1)
ml-faulkner-author-italics.notes: Faulkner describes the use of italics and earlier desired colored inks for Benjy; his retrospective language about disability is period-specific and should not be adopted as clinical terminology.

ml-faulkner-author-title.title: Faulkner at Virginia, transcription of William Faulkner’s discussion of the title from Macbeth (wfaudio26_2)
ml-faulkner-author-title.notes: Faulkner reports choosing the title for its verbal sound and denies a direct intended analogy to Macbeth’s character; distinguish author testimony from broader intertextual literary readings.

ml-faulkner-color-cambridge.title: Jonathan Berliner, Faulkner’s Material Texts, Cambridge University Press blog, 2024
ml-faulkner-color-cambridge.notes: Research-based account of 1929 negotiations over colored ink, typographic marks and the material production of modernist narrative.

ml-faulkner-color-illinois.title: University of Illinois Literature and Languages Library, Faulkner’s The Sound and the Fury As He Realized It? (2012)
ml-faulkner-color-illinois.notes: Folio Society fourteen-color edition produced with Noel Polk and Stephen M. Ross. Editorial reconstruction, not a recovered 1929 author-colored edition.

ml-faulkner-loa.title: Library of America, William Faulkner and The Sound and the Fury: It’s Good That He Didn’t Wait (2010)
ml-faulkner-loa.notes: Ben Wasson editing dispute, Faulkner’s colored-ink wish, historical first-publisher date 7 October 1929. Letters excerpted; original correspondence should be consulted for textual-critical research.

ml-faulkner-norton.title: W. W. Norton, The Sound and the Fury, Norton Critical Edition (2026), publisher description
ml-faulkner-norton.notes: Edition based on Noel Polk’s corrections, annotated by Michael Gorra. The full critical essays and textual apparatus were not consulted through this record.

ml-faulkner-oxford.title: Oxford Research Encyclopedia of Literature, William Faulkner, abstract
ml-faulkner-oxford.notes: High-level literary-historical assessment: Southern modernism, historical change and global influence; no claim of reading the full chapter.

ml-faulkner-farkas.title: Aliz Farkas, The Critical Reception of William Faulkner’s The Sound and the Fury Across Time (2017)
ml-faulkner-farkas.notes: Abstract explicitly discusses shifts from 1929 reception to criticism in the 1950s. Full article not treated as inspected.

ml-faulkner-nobel.title: NobelPrize.org, William Faulkner: Banquet Speech, Stockholm, 10 December 1950
ml-faulkner-nobel.notes: Nobel Prize year 1949; ceremony and banquet speech 1950. This distinguishes the prize year from the presentation date.

ml-faulkner-macbeth.title: Folger Shakespeare Library, Macbeth, Act 5 Scene 5
ml-faulkner-macbeth.notes: Macbeth’s tomorrow soliloquy, source of the title phrase. Literary interpretations beyond title attribution require argument.

ml-faulkner-spark.title: SparkNotes, The Sound and the Fury: Full Book Summary and April Sixth, 1928
ml-faulkner-spark.notes: Secondary cross-check of fictional sequence and sibling name distinctions only; institutional scholarship and the novel take precedence for disputed interpretation.

ml-woolf-window.title: Virginia Woolf, To the Lighthouse (1927), Part I, The Window (first American-edition witness)
ml-woolf-window.notes: Direct primary text for the opening day, child James, Mrs/Mr Ramsay, Tansley, Lily, Bankes, Paul and Minta, nursery, meal, and ending. Wikisource uses an American-edition witness; differences from first British edition matter in word-level textual comparison.

ml-woolf-time.title: Virginia Woolf, To the Lighthouse (1927), Part II, Time Passes (first American-edition witness)
ml-woolf-time.notes: Direct primary text for the empty house, bracketed notices of Mrs Ramsay, Prue and Andrew, wartime absence, Mrs McNab, Mrs Bast, George and restoration. Specific wording may differ in early British editions.

ml-woolf-lighthouse.title: Virginia Woolf, To the Lighthouse (1927), Part III, The Lighthouse (first American-edition witness)
ml-woolf-lighthouse.notes: Direct primary text for Lily, Mr Ramsay, James, Cam, Macalister and his son, the boat, boots, recognition of James, and the last canvas line. Not an edition-independent authority on typography.

ml-woolf-cambridge-form.title: Marina MacKay, Virginia Woolf, To the Lighthouse (1927), in The Cambridge Introduction to the Novel (2010)
ml-woolf-cambridge-form.notes: Authoritative description of the three-part architecture, first-section day, roughly decade-long middle, final morning, Isle of Skye setting and Lily’s role. Do not pretend to have inspected the whole chapter.

ml-woolf-princeton.title: Princeton University Library, Beach & Woolf: Making Modernism (online exhibition)
ml-woolf-princeton.notes: Lists 1927 Hogarth Press publication; describes literary perspectives, gender and the intellectual freedom of self-publishing. Exhibition summary is not a proof of Woolf’s personal intention in each passage.

ml-woolf-cambridge-empire.title: Helen Carr, Virginia Woolf, Empire and Race, Cambridge Companion to Virginia Woolf
ml-woolf-cambridge-empire.notes: Quotes the daughters’ text about Bank of England and Indian Empire, and situates patriarchy/finance/empire as related subjects. Full chapter not claimed to have been read.

ml-woolf-yale.title: Yale Modernism Lab, To the Lighthouse
ml-woolf-yale.notes: Discussion of Lily’s modernist painting, family, multiple consciousnesses, and the war as rupture. Direct page access may fail; no claim of full-page inspection.

ml-woolf-society.title: Virginia Woolf Society of Great Britain, Virginia Woolf: A Short Biography
ml-woolf-society.notes: Records Talland House holidays in St Ives and the novel’s relocated Isle of Skye setting; biographical family history and death of Julia Stephen in 1895. Biographical source, not proof of fictional identity.

ml-woolf-cambridge-chronology.title: Cambridge Companion to Virginia Woolf (2010), author chronology
ml-woolf-cambridge-chronology.notes: Chronology lists composition started 8 January 1926, British publication 5 May 1927, and 1928 Prix Femina. Preview is a partial book, not complete analysis.

ml-woolf-smith.title: Smith College Libraries, Woolf in the World: Page Proofs of To the Lighthouse
ml-woolf-smith.notes: Catalogs corrections in Woolf’s handwriting on 1927 page proofs; documents her roles as writer, editor and publisher. Specific American editorial interventions must be checked against proofs.

ml-woolf-mendelson.title: Edward Mendelson, Virginia Woolf: To the Lighthouse, Texts and Scanned Images (textual collation)
ml-woolf-mendelson.notes: Comparison of 1927 US/UK editions, the 1930 revised British impression, proof and section-number variants. Some editorial prescriptions are Mendelson’s judgments; do not flatten contested textual judgments into consensus.

ml-woolf-nyrb-editions.title: Mark Hussey, James Heffernan, Edward Mendelson, Respecting Second Thoughts, New York Review of Books (2023)
ml-woolf-nyrb-editions.notes: Illustrates disagreement over the final emotional vantage of The Window and the first American/British variants. Treat the ending as focalization open to argument, not a narrator-certified fact.

ml-woolf-npg.title: National Portrait Gallery, Virginia Woolf
ml-woolf-npg.notes: Institutional summary of Woolf’s role in modernist fiction and Bloomsbury; a general assessment, not evidence of direct influence on specific later novelists.

ml-borges-prh.title: Penguin Random House, Collected Fictions (Andrew Hurley), publisher table of contents and author
ml-borges-prh.notes: Publisher records both sections, all seventeen stories in the expanded collection, English titling, and author bio. It does not reproduce a verified 1944 first printing.

ml-borges-openlibrary.title: Open Library, Ficciones (1956), edition contents and publication record
ml-borges-openlibrary.notes: Records 1956 expanded table of contents; records translated/edition variants; not an account of narrative plot.

ml-borges-cambridge-i.title: Steven Boldy, Fictions Part I: The Garden of Forking Paths (1941), A Companion to Jorge Luis Borges
ml-borges-cambridge-i.notes: Publisher-visible description covers Pierre Menard and context after Borges’s 1938 accident; no claim to have read the entire chapter.

ml-borges-cambridge-ii.title: Steven Boldy, Fictions Part II: Artifices (1944), A Companion to Jorge Luis Borges
ml-borges-cambridge-ii.notes: Public description details narrator, setting, accident, memory and documentary frame of Funes, His Memory. Other chapter contents are not represented as inspected.

ml-borges-fiddian.title: Robin Fiddian, Pierre Menard, autor del Quijote: Contexts, Antecedents, Lines of Enquiry, Romance Studies (2021)
ml-borges-fiddian.notes: Open article on 1939 Sur publication, fictional critic, authorship, war setting, Cervantine precursor, and history of criticism. Interpretive proposals remain proposals.

ml-borges-buffalo.title: University at Buffalo Capen Chair, Painting Borges: guide to key stories
ml-borges-buffalo.notes: University teaching/exhibition guide; detailed synopses for Garden of Forking Paths and Circular Ruins; not a critical edition of Borges’s Spanish.

ml-borges-spark-garden.title: SparkNotes, The Garden of Forking Paths, full plot summary
ml-borges-spark-garden.notes: Secondary summary of Yu Tsun, Madden, Stephen Albert, Tsui Pen, motive, murder and coded newspaper message; check interpretation separately.

ml-borges-encyc-circular.title: Encyclopedia.com, The Circular Ruins study entry
ml-borges-encyc-circular.notes: Secondary plot and first-publication account for Circular Ruins; not a primary textual witness.

ml-borges-litcharts.title: LitCharts, Ficciones summary and story index
ml-borges-litcharts.notes: Provides plot synopsis for Secret Miracle, Three Versions Judas, Death and Compass and sections of collection; selected story coverage may be restricted.

ml-borges-ebsco-sword.title: EBSCO Research Starters, The Shape of the Sword by Jorge Luis Borges
ml-borges-ebsco-sword.notes: Checks sword/scar framing, British soldiers, John Vincent Moon betrayal and final reveal.

ml-borges-litcharts-traitor.title: LitCharts, Ficciones: Theme of the Traitor and the Hero, summary and analysis
ml-borges-litcharts-traitor.notes: Corroborates Ryan, Fergus Kilpatrick, Nolan, Shakespeare allusions and staged public assassination.

ml-borges-compass.title: Lecturia, Death and the Compass, story summary and analysis
ml-borges-compass.notes: Checks Lonnrot’s rhombus, Triste-le-Roy, Scharlach’s revenge and purpose of staged signs; no claim of scholarly peer review.

ml-borges-oeis.title: OEIS A392510, number of possible texts in Borges’s Library of Babel
ml-borges-oeis.notes: Gives alphabet of 25 signs, 410 pages, 40 lines/page, 80 signs/line, 25^(1,312,000) distinct full-length volumes; distinct texts finite despite spatially infinite gallery possibility.

ml-borges-gothenburg-phoenix.title: Anders Johansson, Borges Beyond Interpretations: Changeability and Form in La secta del Fénix, Borges Center

ml-borges-sfe.title: Science Fiction Encyclopedia, Jorge Luis Borges
ml-borges-sfe.notes: Confirms 1941 precursors, 1944 fourteen-piece Ficciones, 1956 expansion by three, 1962 English-language collections; broad editorial assessment of importance.

ml-borges-oxford.title: Edwin Williamson, Borges’s Reception in Europe and the USA, Oxford Handbook of Jorge Luis Borges (2024)
ml-borges-oxford.notes: Accessible abstract describes transformative reception by postwar writers, poststructuralist/postmodern appropriation and later contextual scholarship. Does not establish particular influence without a further source.

ml-borges-approach.title: The Approach to Al-Mu’tasim, synopsis of invented novel and review
ml-borges-approach.notes: Summarizes hypothetical Bahadur Ali editions, student’s journey after riot, and quest for a spiritual source. Independent publisher table supports inclusion but not this plot.

ml-borges-end.title: The End (Borges short story): publication and plot overview
ml-borges-end.notes: Supports 1953 first publication, 1956 inclusion, relation to Martin Fierro and killing by Black guitarist. Not independent critical scholarship.

ml-borges-five.title: The Fifth Desk, Ficciones, contents and critical essay
ml-borges-five.notes: Independent interpretive account of 1944 vs 1956 contents, The South’s double reading, and some 1961-62 reception; used as secondary, not a sole bibliographic authority.

ml-beckett-primary.title: Samuel Beckett, En attendant Godot (Les Éditions de Minuit, 1952); Waiting for Godot (Grove Press, 1954; Faber & Faber, 1956)
ml-beckett-primary.notes: Primary copyrighted script; catalog/publisher page is bibliographic orientation only and is not the complete text. These drafts are original teaching prose, not a collation of all editions.

ml-beckett-cambridge-graver.title: Lawrence Graver, Beckett: Waiting for Godot, chapter Godot in French and in English (Cambridge University Press)
ml-beckett-cambridge-graver.notes: Dates of composition, French print and premiere, authorial translation; publisher excerpt accessible. Does not justify invented line-by-line variants.

ml-beckett-cambridge-mcdonald.title: Ronan McDonald, The Cambridge Introduction to Samuel Beckett, chapter Plays (Cambridge University Press, 2007)
ml-beckett-cambridge-mcdonald.notes: Discusses the minimal setting, Godot as possible religious figure, sheep/goats allusion, and postwar readings; these are critical interpretations, not settled textual identities.

ml-beckett-cambridge-morin.title: Emilie Morin, Theatre of the Absurd, in The Cambridge Companion to Modernist Theatre (2025)
ml-beckett-cambridge-morin.notes: Historically contextualizes Esslin’s critical rubric and the political and transnational breadth of experimental drama; abstract only.

ml-beckett-utah-festival.title: Utah Shakespeare Festival, Waiting for Godot: About the Playwright
ml-beckett-utah-festival.notes: Outlines two acts, recurring boy, Pozzo’s blindness, and the changed tree; bibliography/production date in this guide should be cross-checked with Cambridge.

ml-beckett-sparknotes.title: SparkNotes, Waiting for Godot: Full Play Summary
ml-beckett-sparknotes.notes: Basic two-act sequence, Pozzo’s intended sale of Lucky, boy’s messages, no departures. Secondary, not a substitute for edition-level textual comparison.

ml-beckett-reading-staging.title: University of Reading, Staging Beckett: Waiting for Godot, Module 1
ml-beckett-reading-staging.notes: 1953 Paris and 1955 London staging history, reception, director Peter Hall, critics Hobson and Tynan, and performance conditions.

ml-beckett-washu.title: Washington University Libraries, Samuel Beckett Papers
ml-beckett-washu.notes: Records 1975 Berlin production notebook holdings and related Cluchey materials; collection descriptions, not a full text of notebooks.

ml-beckett-emory.title: Emory University, Index to Samuel Beckett Letters: Warten auf Godot
ml-beckett-emory.notes: Documents Berlin production under Beckett, 1975 rehearsal/premiere, correspondence links; index metadata rather than complete letters.

ml-beckett-morgan.title: Morgan Library & Museum, Justice: Samuel Beckett’s Waiting for Godot
ml-beckett-morgan.notes: Documents prison stagings and Rick Cluchey reception; makes an interpretive comparison to prison limbo.

ml-beckett-depaul.title: DePaul University Special Collections, Samuel Beckett Collection and San Quentin Drama Workshop
ml-beckett-depaul.notes: 1957 San Quentin performance and Rick Cluchey’s subsequent theatrical work and connection to Beckett.

ml-beckett-npg.title: National Portrait Gallery, Samuel Beckett display archive
ml-beckett-npg.notes: 1955 London premiere and divided critical reception; calls the play a postwar theatrical landmark.

ml-beckett-esslin.title: Martin Esslin, The Theatre of the Absurd (Doubleday, 1961)
ml-beckett-esslin.notes: Author and 1961 edition, critics’ label. No claim to have examined full copyrighted critical monograph.

ml-beckett-british-library.title: Open British National Bibliography, Waiting for Godot revised/unexpurgated English edition
ml-beckett-british-library.notes: 1971 educational edition notes revised and unexpurgated English published in 1965; supports British textual history.

ml-eliot-primary-1922.title: T. S. Eliot, The Waste Land, original 1922 book text with Eliot’s Notes, Wikisource transcription
ml-eliot-primary-1922.notes: Evidence for the five movements, recurring images, voice sequences and original author notes; this 1922 *book* text is not the unannotated Criterion/Dial magazine state. Read beside a verified facsimile for word-for-word textual claims.

ml-eliot-rpo.title: University of Toronto, Representative Poetry Online, The Waste Land, annotated text
ml-eliot-rpo.notes: Primary poem plus editorial commentary and cross-references on allusions, including Upanishadic thunder; later scholarly glosses must be distinguished from Eliot’s own Notes.

ml-eliot-poetry-primary.title: Poetry Foundation, T. S. Eliot, The Waste Land (poem)
ml-eliot-poetry-primary.notes: Readable poem with contemporary educational explanatory apparatus. Copyright statements vary by jurisdiction; manuscripts do not reproduce long passages.

ml-eliot-poetry-guide.title: Tyler Malone, T. S. Eliot: The Waste Land, Poetry Foundation, 2023
ml-eliot-poetry-guide.notes: Guide to movement structure, references to poetry and popular culture, the typist, Phlebas, and the fifth movement. Interpretations are indicated as such.

ml-eliot-cambridge-century.title: The Waste Land after One Hundred Years, Cambridge University Press, scholarly introduction, 2022

ml-eliot-yale-centennial.title: Yale Beinecke Library, Celebrating The Waste Land’s Centennial, 2022
ml-eliot-yale-centennial.notes: Publishing negotiations involving Eliot, Pound, Scofield Thayer, The Dial; magazine and first-edition materials; evidence of divergent initial reception.

ml-eliot-bl-drafts.title: British Library, T. S. Eliot’s The Waste Land: drafts and annotations
ml-eliot-bl-drafts.notes: Pound’s and Vivien Eliot’s annotations, 1922 manuscript revision, changing structure. The exhibit is not a complete collation of drafts.

ml-eliot-cambridge-scofield.title: Martin Scofield, The Waste Land (1922), in T. S. Eliot: The Poems, Cambridge University Press
ml-eliot-cambridge-scofield.notes: Fragmentary composition, Pound’s editorial contribution and facsimile edited by Valerie Eliot in 1971; chapter full text not claimed inspected.

ml-eliot-poetry-exhibit.title: Poetry Foundation, Better Craftsmen, Not Gods: a Waste Land manuscript exhibit
ml-eliot-poetry-exhibit.notes: Manuscript history, collaborative making, contextual questions of prejudice and literary canon; exhibit provides thoughtful critical framing, not evidence that any single 1922 poem line is a documentary statement.

ml-eliot-ulysses-essay.title: T. S. Eliot, Ulysses, Order, and Myth, The Dial, November 1923 (documentary excerpt)
ml-eliot-ulysses-essay.notes: Documents Eliot’s later published statement of the mythic method and regard for Joyce; not a primary record of the private planning of The Waste Land.

ml-eliot-kings-centennial.title: King’s College Cambridge, The Waste Land at 100, archive exhibition
ml-eliot-kings-centennial.notes: Original Criterion and Dial pages, 1922 US book and early British printing, dated bibliographical evidence; day-of-publication dating has variant accounts.

ml-eliot-1971-facsimile.title: Valerie Eliot, ed., The Waste Land: A Facsimile and Transcript of the Original Drafts, 1971
ml-eliot-1971-facsimile.notes: Identifies the edited book documenting manuscript and annotations; neither full facsimile nor its complete readings were inspected for this draft.

ml-eliot-yale-lecture.title: Open Yale Courses, Modern Poetry ENGL 310, Lecture 11: T. S. Eliot
ml-eliot-yale-lecture.notes: Scholarly teaching account of the final movement, water, myth, and the three ethical instructions; interpretive secondary source.

ml-eliot-anthology-uva.title: University of Virginia anthology, The Waste Land (1922) historical text and textual apparatus
ml-eliot-anthology-uva.notes: Search index excerpts verify line sequence; full browser open was restricted, so this edition was not directly collated. Prefer other primary sources for line-level review.

ml-rushdie-edition.title: Salman Rushdie, Midnight’s Children (Jonathan Cape, 1981); Random House edition bibliographic listing
ml-rushdie-edition.notes: Primary work to consult for definitive text and exact wording; copyrighted novel was not systematically collated against a specified full edition during this drafting pass. Original secondary plot summaries are explicitly identified.

ml-rushdie-ebsco.title: Lydia Forssander-Song, Midnight’s Children by Salman Rushdie, EBSCO Research Starters (2021)

ml-rushdie-sparknotes.title: SparkNotes, Midnight’s Children Full Book Summary

ml-rushdie-booker.title: The Booker Prizes, Midnight’s Children, winner of the 1981 Booker Prize

ml-rushdie-booker-quarter.title: The Booker Prizes, The Booker of Bookers

ml-rushdie-booker-forty.title: The Booker Prizes, The Best of the Booker (2008)
ml-rushdie-booker-forty.notes: Documents 2008 public vote and award, separate from the earlier Booker of Bookers.

ml-rushdie-cambridge-partition.title: A History of the Indian Novel in English, “Handcuffed to History”: Partition and the Indian Novel in English
ml-rushdie-cambridge-partition.notes: Treats Rushdie within older Indian writing about Partition and the coexistence of independence and violence; full scholarly chapter not claimed read.

ml-rushdie-cambridge-novel.title: Marina MacKay, “Salman Rushdie, Midnight’s Children (1981),” The Cambridge Introduction to the Novel (2012)
ml-rushdie-cambridge-novel.notes: Novel, nation, and narration; visible excerpt notes the self-correcting narrator and links to Tristram Shandy, not a claim of a complete chapter reading.

ml-rushdie-emergency-oup.title: The Indian Emergency (1975–1977) in Historical Perspective, Oxford University Press

ml-rushdie-emergency-pib.title: Government of India Press Information Bureau, The Emergency in India: historical factsheet (2025)

ml-rushdie-bangladesh-archives.title: UK National Archives Education, The Independence of Bangladesh in 1971

ml-camus-edition.title: Albert Camus, L’Étranger (Gallimard, 1942); Albert Camus Society bibliographic record

ml-camus-stanford.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, Albert Camus (2011, revised 2021)

ml-camus-classicslaunch.title: Classics Library, The Stranger: synopsis and bibliographic context
